snippet.title: How El Niño Impacts the Atlantic and Pacific 2026 Hurricane Season
snippet.description:
El Niño is likely to emerge very soon this summer heading into June after Memorial Day as equatorial Pacific sea surface temperatures continue to warm. What exactly does this mean for hurricane season, which starts on June 1st in the Atlantic?

PACIFIC OCEAN... Usually points towards more hurricanes thanks to warmer SSTs. All of this warmth wants to rise, which can fuel hurricanes. The season has already started in this Basin on May 15th. 

ATLANTIC OCEAN... Usually points towards less hurricanes thanks to increased upper-level winds aiding in vertical wind shear. This is what you would want for tornadoes, but quite the opposite for hurricanes as it shreds them apart. This is due to the strengthening of the subtropical jetsream, which is supplying those upper-level winds. 

The National Hurricane Center is predicting a below average season, but all it takes is one storm! Like and follow for more for 10 Days of Hurricane Preparedness starting tomorrow.

snippet.title: Why Everyone Got Spain’s Blackout Wrong
snippet.description:
Prof Janusz Bialek explains the real causes on the Iberian blackout (Spain and Portugal).

On April 28, 2025, the Iberian power grid collapsed into darkness; but not because of a power shortage. The voltage was actually rising. So, how does that happen? I sat down with my Imperial College colleague, Prof. Janusz Bialek, to cut through the internet rumours and look at the official investigation behind this unprecedented blackout. We discuss what triggered the instability, why the grid couldn't stop it, and whether the popular claim that renewable energy is to blame is actually true. The reality is much more interesting!

snippet.title: 20 must-have emergency items for your car
snippet.description:
September is National Preparedness Month — an annual campaign that reminds us all that taking time to prepare for emergencies and disasters can help keep ourselves, our families and our communities safe.

Whether you are heading out on a scenic fall road trip to the East Coast or just upgraded your ride to a more family-friendly SUV, being prepared before you hit the road is key. Lenexa’s Emergency Preparedness Manager Susan McMahan shares 20 essential items every vehicle should have to stay safe, mobile and ready for the unexpected.

“Preparedness is more than just a checklist — it’s a mindset,” said McMahan. “Whether you’re at home, at work or on the road, having the right tools and resources on hand can turn a crisis into a manageable situation.”

1. Basic first-aid kit
From bandages and ibuprofen to disposable gloves and ice packs, a first-aid kit is crucial for treating minor injuries on the go.

2. Car escape tool
A seatbelt cutter and tempered glass window breaker can be lifesaving in case of an accident or entrapment.

3. Car jack
Most vehicles come with a jack, but it’s important to know how to use it safely in case of a flat tire.

4. Spare tire or emergency inflator 
Always keep a properly inflated spare tire in your vehicle and inspect it regularly for signs of wear or damage. Alternatively, you can carry an emergency tire inflator aerosol. But remember, this is only a temporary fix designed to help you reach the nearest tire repair facility safely. 

5. Cell phone charger
A dead phone can leave you stranded. Pack an extra charger — or better yet, a portable battery bank.

6. Thermal blanket
These aluminum-lined blankets reflect up to 90% of body heat and offer critical warmth in cold weather or during an emergency overnight stay.

7. Waterproof ponchos
Military-grade rain ponchos will keep you warm and dry if you’re stuck outside during heavy rain.

8. Work gloves
Durable gloves protect your hands while handling repairs, changing tires or moving debris.

9. Water bottles
Always keep at least a couple of sealed water bottles in your car. Staying hydrated is vital during long delays or breakdowns.

10. Nonperishable food
Energy bars, trail mix or vacuum-sealed snacks can be a lifesaver if you’re stranded without access to food.

11. Compact shovel
A foldable or multiuse shovel can help you dig through snow, sand or mud to get your vehicle back on the road.

12. Whistle
A loud whistle is an easy way to attract attention if your voice can’t carry far in an emergency.

13. Ice scraper/snow brush
A sturdy scraper and brush combo helps you clear frost, snow or ice quickly to restore visibility and stay safe in winter weather.

14. Reflective triangle or flares
If your car breaks down, place a reflective triangle or emergency flares behind it to alert other drivers and keep yourself safe.

15. Paper map or road atlas
In case you lose GPS or cell signal, a paper map can help you navigate unfamiliar routes.

16. Cat litter or sand
A bag of cat litter or sand can provide much-needed traction if you get stuck on ice or in mud.

17. Flashlight (with extra batteries)
A reliable flashlight helps you see under the hood or change a tire after dark — and can also signal for help.

18. Duct tape
From temporary car fixes to sealing a broken window, duct tape is a multipurpose tool that earns its place in any emergency kit.

19. Multitool
A sturdy multitool can serve as a screwdriver, knife or pliers — all in one compact device.

20. Notebook and pen
Helpful for taking notes in case of an accident, exchanging information or jotting down directions.

snippet.title: This Tornado Hurricane Safety Hack Could Save Your Child’s Life 💔
snippet.description:
Tornado season is no joke — and every parent needs a plan 👶💨
Here’s how I prepare my child just in case something happens.

1️⃣ ID Band Trick 🩹
Write your child’s name, age, and your phone number on a band-aid and stick it to their arm — just in case you get separated.

2️⃣ Emergency Backpack 🎒
Pack a small backpack with wireless earbuds, a phone, water, snacks, and essential items.

3️⃣ Hidden Cash & Card 💵💳
Place a few bills and a backup bank card under your child’s shoe insole — it’s safe and easy to reach later.

Simple, smart, and could make all the difference. 💛
Stay safe, stay prepared. 🌪️

snippet.title: TU mochila de 72 horas está al revés: el orden 3-3-3-3 del protocolo SERE
snippet.description:
El 28 de abril de 2025, a las 12:33, 36 millones de personas se quedaron sin luz en España y Portugal. Mucha gente sacó ese día su mochila de emergencia y descubrió que la tenía montada del revés.

No va de qué metes. Va de EN QUÉ ORDEN, y casi nadie lo cuenta.

En el entrenamiento militar de supervivencia se usa la regla 3-3-3-3: tres minutos sin aire, tres horas sin refugio, tres días sin agua y tres semanas sin comida. Es una regla para memorizar el ORDEN DE URGENCIA. Y si tu cuerpo falla en ese orden, tu mochila debería estar montada en ese orden.

La mayoría la organiza por categorías, como un armario: la comida por un lado, la ropa por otro, el botiquín por otro. Resultado: lo que necesitas en los primeros minutos está en el fondo, y lo que no vas a tocar en tres semanas te queda arriba y a mano.

En este vídeo reordenamos la mochila que YA TIENES en cuatro capas, de la tapa al fondo. Veinte minutos, cero euros, no hay que comprar nada.

⏱️ CAPÍTULOS
0:00 El apagón del 28-A y la mochila del revés
1:05 La regla 3-3-3-3 del protocolo SERE
2:13 CAPA 1 · Aire — 3 minutos (y por qué va arriba del todo)
3:40 CAPA 2 · Refugio — 3 horas (el error más común de todos)
4:57 CAPA 3 · Agua — 3 días (por qué cargar 4,5 litros es un error)
6:14 CAPA 4 · Comida — 3 semanas (va al fondo, y va poca)
7:07 La QUINTA capa que no está en la regla
7:57 Repaso de las cuatro capas + cómo rehacerla hoy

⚠️ UNA ACLARACIÓN DE SEGURIDAD
Una mascarilla FFP2 filtra partículas: humo, polvo, ceniza y escombro en suspensión. NO te da oxígeno y NO te protege de los gases. En un incendio con humo denso lo que te salva es agacharte rápido, porque el humo sube, y salir de ahí cuanto antes. Por ahí circula mucha desinformación con esto.

📌 SI TE FALTA LA BASE, EMPIEZA POR AQUÍ

If you think your bed is just for sleeping, think again… because this bed can actually save your life during an earthquake!
Meet the Earthquake Protection Bed — a revolutionary invention designed to instantly protect you the moment disaster strikes. The second its ultra-sensitive sensors detect tremors, the top frame opens in a split second and slides you into a reinforced steel survival chamber. This chamber is built to withstand collapsing walls, heavy debris, and even concrete blocks.

Once inside, the lid automatically seals shut, keeping you safe from harm. Inside, you’ll find oxygen tanks, fresh drinking water, food supplies, and first-aid kits — everything you need to survive for days if needed. And to keep you calm and entertained, it even has a built-in TV, so you can stay informed until rescue teams arrive.

It’s like having your own personal survival bunker… hidden right in your bedroom. This is not just a bed — it’s your ultimate life-saving shelter.
